# Contribute {.unnumbered}

The book is written in the open. Both language trees, the bibliography, the
figure sources, and the reader that renders them live in one repository,
[latere-ai/ai-as-an-infrastructure](https://github.com/latere-ai/ai-as-an-infrastructure),
and every chapter ends with two links into it: one opens an issue about that
chapter, the other opens the editor on the file the chapter is compiled from.

A book about a field that moves this fast goes out of date in public. Readers
are the ones who notice, usually while reading the sentence that is wrong.

## What helps most

- Factual corrections, with a primary source. A paper, a specification, a
  vendor document, or a release note carries the argument further than a
  recollection does.
- Numbers that have gone stale. Context lengths, prices, throughputs, and model
  names age fastest, and the chapter that quotes one should say when it was
  true.
- Passages that are unclear. A chapter that lost you at a particular paragraph
  is a defect worth reporting even when nothing in it is false, and saying
  where the thread broke is enough.
- Typos, broken links, math that fails to render, diagrams that come out wrong.
- The English and Chinese pages disagreeing. They are meant to say the same
  thing, so a gap between them is a bug in one of the two.

Reports are welcome in either language. If a question is easier to ask than to
file, every page carries a comment thread at its foot.

## Sending a change

For a small fix, "Edit this page" at the foot of a chapter opens its source in
GitHub's editor, and a pull request follows from the same screen. For anything
larger, the repository's
[contributing guide](https://github.com/latere-ai/ai-as-an-infrastructure/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
covers the layout, the writing rules, and the build. Two of them matter more
than the rest: a change to one language needs the same change in the other, and
the build is the test, so it has to compile both.

The content is licensed
[CC BY-NC-ND 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/), which
means a rewrite of prose for its own sake cannot be merged. Corrections,
clarifications, and repairs can, and they are the point.
